subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated GPU reservation & isolation needs (Aurora Biosystems)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@aurorabio.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated GPU reservation & isolation needs (Aurora Biosystems)

Hi Sofia — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Latency instability during peak batch jobs (affects clinical inference pipelines).
- PHI/data residency concerns — need tenant isolation and customer-managed keying.
- Predictable unit economics: want a plan to cap per-token cost and avoid surprise bursts.

Primary goals we captured:
- Dedicated, isolated serving for PHI workloads (no multi-tenant co-located inference).
- P99 latency target: <= 250 ms for 512-token requests, typical SLA target 99.9% uptime.
- Sustained throughput: ~600 small-to-mid requests / minute with ability to burst to 1.5x.
- Auditability: logs and access trails for each inference request (for compliance).

What we propose (high level):
- Reserved GPU pool (dedicated tenancy) tied to a single customer project; hardware options: 2x A100-80GB baseline, burst to 4x H100 in peak windows (engineering to size precisely).
- Network/VPC isolation + integration with customer KMS/HSM for key control.
- Autoscaling policy with burst buckets and throttling thresholds; prefix/KV caching to reduce repeated token cost.
- SLAs: 99.9% uptime for serving control plane + target P99 latency SLO; escalation path with 15-min response for Sev1.
- Compliance artifacts: SOC2 scoping and audit log export available for ingestion.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_onepager.pdf (one-page summary of Dedicated offering).

Immediate next steps / owners:
1) Technical discovery call to map request size distribution and token profile — owner: Jordan Blake — target week of 6/15.
2) Security questionnaire and KMS integration checklist — owner: Markus Klein — ask: share existing KMS contact and required compliance docs by 6/12.
3) Draft SOW and cost estimate for two sizing options (baseline and peak) — owner: Hannah Schmitt — target draft by 6/16.
4) Procurement intro — Hannah to loop in Aurora procurement contact and share sample contract redlines.

Questions for you (if you can answer inline):
- Do you have preferred GPU type constraints (e.g., company policy that rules out A100/H100)?
- Any blackout windows for upgrades or maintenance we should avoid?
- Who should be the procurement point of contact for contract redlines?

Thanks again — we’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the technical discovery.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Thanks Hannah — helpful recap. A few clarifications and answers inline below.

> Do you have preferred GPU type constraints?
We don’t have a strict ban on A100/H100 but our internal infra team prefers H100 where latency-sensitive models run. That said cost matters — keen to see two options as you suggested.

> Any blackout windows for upgrades or maintenance?
We run nightly batch jobs 02:00–05:00 PT on weekdays; please avoid major infra changes during that window.

> Who should be the procurement POC?
Procurement is procurement@aurorabio.com (cc’ing here). I’m including a VCF with our procurement lead in case you want to start NDAs/SOW redline exchange.

Extra ask from our side:
- Can you include a short appendix in the SOW about data retention policy and log export cadence?
- Do you provide a way to pin model versions for rollouts and automated rollback if latency regresses?

We’re generally excited to progress — happy to do the technical discovery next week.

Thanks,
Sofia Ramos
Head of ML Ops, Aurora Biosystems
sofia.ramos@aurorabio.com | +1 (617) 555-3467

Quick internal note after Sofia’s answers — draft action plan from infra/solutions: 

Sizing / options to include in SOW:
- Option A (cost-conservative): 2x A100-80GB nodes, fixed reserved slots, expected sustained throughput ~600 rpm, burst to 1.2x.
- Option B (latency-first): 2x H100 baseline + 2x H100 burst nodes (pre-warmed), target P99 <= 200–250 ms for 512 tokens.

Technical asks for discovery call (Jordan):
- Request distribution (tokens/request histogram), typical prompt/context sizes, and model family(s) you plan to serve.
- Expected KV cache hit rate for repeated prompts (if any).

Compliance/ops notes (Markus):
- We can integrate with Aurora KMS; need contact and public key details.
- Audit log export: daily batch S3 export + near-real-time webhook for critical events.

Timeline proposal:
- 6/12: Security questionnaire kickoff (Markus owns).
- 6/15–6/18: Technical discovery (Jordan owns; schedule with Aurora).
- 6/16: Draft SOW & two costed options (Hannah owns) — aim to share for internal review.
- 6/22: Proposal review and procurement sync.

Please confirm owners and I’ll start a short cost model to validate both options (rough 30-min estimate to generate base numbers). Also note: avoid any maintenance work 02:00–05:00 PT per Aurora.

-Markus
